title: 8 Best Financial Consolidation Software Tools in 2026
summary: Compare the 8 best financial consolidation software tools in 2026, from OneStream and Oracle to AI agents like Concourse, by consolidation depth, fit, and cost.
body_markdown:
For any company with more than one entity, the group close is where the month-end really gets hard: combining ledgers across subsidiaries, eliminating intercompany transactions, translating currencies, and producing consolidated financials that tie out and hold up to audit. Financial consolidation software exists to automate that, replacing the fragile consolidation spreadsheet that only one person understands with a controlled, repeatable process.


The category runs from enterprise EPM platforms built for the most complex global groups to mid-market tools and, increasingly, AI agents that automate the surrounding work. This guide compares the eight best financial consolidation software tools in 2026, what each is best at, who it fits, and where it falls short, so you can match the tool to the complexity of your close.


## **What is the best financial consolidation software?**


> The best financial consolidation software in 2026 is OneStream, Oracle, CCH Tagetik, and SAP Group Reporting for enterprise group consolidation, Planful and Prophix for mid-market consolidation plus FP&A, and Board for consolidation inside a planning platform, with AI agents like Concourse automating the intercompany reconciliation, close, and consolidated reporting around them.


> **Concourse is the AI-agent layer on this list.** It does not replace a consolidation engine; instead, its autonomous agents connect to your ERPs and systems to run the work *around* consolidation, matching and reconciling intercompany transactions, driving the close, and producing consolidated reporting and analysis, with every number traceable back to source. It is built for teams that want AI to take on the manual close work, alongside their consolidation tool.


## **How we evaluated financial consolidation software**


Consolidation tools differ most by the complexity they are built for. We compared them across the criteria that decide the fit:


- **Consolidation depth.** Multi-entity, multi-currency consolidation, intercompany eliminations, ownership and minority interest, and complex group structures.
- **Close management.** Task workflows, journal entries, and controls around the group close.
- **Reporting.** Consolidated statutory and management reporting on top of the numbers.
- **Data connectivity.** How well it pulls from multiple ERPs and source systems.
- **AI and automation.** From rules-based automation to AI agents that run the reconciliation and close work.
- **Fit and ideal size.** From mid-market groups to the largest, most complex global enterprises.

## **The 8 best financial consolidation software tools in 2026**


### **1. Concourse, Best for AI Agents Around the Consolidation Process**


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. It is not a consolidation engine, and that distinction matters: rather than performing statutory eliminations and currency translation itself, its agents connect to your ERPs, data warehouse, and source systems and automate the manual work that surrounds consolidation, matching and reconciling intercompany transactions, driving close tasks, and producing consolidated reporting and analysis.


For multi-entity teams, intercompany is where the group close bogs down, and it is exactly the kind of high-volume, repetitive matching agents handle well. Concourse runs that work end to end, and every output traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which is what makes it defensible to an auditor. It is SOC 2 Type II certified, connects to 100+ systems, and meets teams in ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email. Concourse reports customers cutting manual work by roughly 75% and saving 20+ hours per user per month. See our guide to[intercompany reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/intercompany-reconciliation) for how this works.


**Best for.** Multi-entity teams that want AI agents to automate intercompany reconciliation, close, and consolidated reporting alongside their consolidation tool.


**Keep in mind.** Concourse is an execution and analysis layer, not a dedicated consolidation engine. For statutory multi-currency consolidation with eliminations and ownership accounting, pair it with one of the platforms below and use Concourse to automate the reconciliation, close, and reporting around it.


### **2. OneStream, Best for Unified Enterprise Consolidation**


OneStream is the category leader for enterprise financial consolidation and close, unifying consolidation, planning, and reporting on one platform for large, complex global organizations. Founded in 2010, it was[taken private by Hg for $6.4 billion in a deal completed in April 2026](https://www.cfodive.com/news/onestream-closes-64b-go-private-deal-hg/816799/) . It is the standard for the most demanding group closes.


**Best for.** Large enterprises that want deep, unified consolidation, close, and reporting on a single platform.


**Keep in mind.** It carries enterprise weight and cost, and is more than most mid-market groups need for consolidation alone.


### **3. Oracle, Best for Oracle-Ecosystem Consolidation**


Oracle offers consolidation through its cloud[Financial Consolidation and Close (FCCS)](https://www.us-analytics.com/hyperionblog/faq-oracle-financial-consolidation-and-close-cloud-service-fccs) service, part of Oracle EPM Cloud, alongside the legacy on-prem Hyperion Financial Management (HFM). Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) is deep and proven, and the natural choice for organizations already standardized on Oracle ERP and EPM.


**Best for.** Large enterprises embedded in the Oracle ERP/EPM ecosystem.


**Keep in mind.** It is at its best inside the Oracle stack; standalone, it is a heavy enterprise commitment.


### **4. CCH Tagetik, Best for Enterprise CPM + Statutory Reporting**


CCH Tagetik is a mature enterprise corporate performance management platform strong in consolidation paired with statutory and regulatory reporting. Tagetik, founded in 1986, was[acquired by Wolters Kluwer for €300 million in 2017](https://www.wolterskluwer.com/en/news/wolters-kluwer-agreement-acquisition-tagetik) and sits within its Corporate Performance Solutions unit. It is a common pick where consolidation and complex regulatory reporting go hand in hand.


**Best for.** Enterprises that need consolidation together with heavy statutory and regulatory reporting.


**Keep in mind.** It is a full enterprise CPM platform, with the implementation effort that implies.


### **5. SAP Group Reporting, Best for SAP-Ecosystem Consolidation**


SAP delivers consolidation through SAP S/4HANA Finance for Group Reporting, its strategic go-forward solution, alongside the legacy SAP Business Planning and Consolidation (BPC). For organizations standardized on SAP S/4HANA, running consolidation natively in the same platform as the ledger is the draw. SAP SE trades on the NYSE (ticker SAP) and Frankfurt.


**Best for.** Enterprises standardized on SAP S/4HANA that want consolidation native to their ERP.


**Keep in mind.** Its advantage is tied to the SAP ecosystem; the transition from legacy BPC to Group Reporting is a real project.


### **6. Planful, Best for Mid-Market Consolidation + FP&A**


Planful is a cloud FP&A and financial performance management platform whose consolidation strength pairs naturally with its planning and reporting. Founded in 2000 as Host Analytics and rebranded to Planful in 2020, it is[owned by Vector Capital](https://www.vectorcapital.com/investments/case-study/planful) . It is a frequent step up for mid-market groups that outgrow spreadsheet consolidation.


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise groups that want consolidation and FP&A on one platform.


**Keep in mind.** For the most complex global consolidation, the enterprise EPM tools go deeper.


### **7. Prophix, Best for Mid-Market CPM**


Prophix offers consolidation within a unified mid-market corporate performance management suite covering budgeting, forecasting, close, and reporting. Founded in 1987 in Ontario with 3,000+ customers, it is[majority-owned by Hg](https://hgcapital.com/insights/hg-invests-in-prophix-to-continue-to-scale-the-business-and-invest-further) . It is a strong single-vendor pick for mid-market groups.


**Best for.** Mid-market companies that want consolidation as part of one CPM platform.


**Keep in mind.** It has a more traditional CPM feel and is aimed at the mid-market rather than the largest global enterprises.


### **8. Board, Best for Consolidation Inside a Planning Platform**


Board (BOARD International) combines financial consolidation with planning and analytics on a single "decision-making platform." Founded in Switzerland in 1994, it received a[majority investment from Nordic Capital in 2021](https://www.board.com/news/nordic-capital-acquires-board-international-provider-1-decision-making-platform) . It suits teams that want consolidation, planning, and BI unified rather than bought separately.


**Best for.** Mid-market to enterprise teams that want consolidation, planning, and analytics on one platform.


**Keep in mind.** As a broad platform, scope the consolidation capability to your specific group complexity.


*Also worth a look:*[Vena](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-financial-reporting-software) offers lighter, Excel-native consolidation for mid-market teams; Workiva sits above consolidation as a connected reporting and disclosure layer rather than a consolidation engine; and Datarails and Joiin serve smaller groups. We kept the main list to platforms built for the consolidation and close itself.


## **Which financial consolidation software is right for you?**


There is no single best financial consolidation software, only the best fit for the complexity of your group and your existing stack.


- **Choose Concourse** to put AI agents on the intercompany reconciliation, close, and consolidated reporting around your consolidation engine.
- **Choose OneStream** for unified, deep enterprise consolidation and close on one platform.
- **Choose Oracle or SAP** if you are standardized on their ERP/EPM ecosystem.
- **Choose CCH Tagetik** if consolidation and heavy statutory reporting go together.
- **Choose Planful or Prophix** for mid-market consolidation alongside FP&A.
- **Choose Board** if you want consolidation, planning, and analytics unified.


The clearest shift in 2026 is that the consolidation *engine* and the work *around* it are separating. The enterprise platforms own the eliminations and currency translation; the AI-agent layer increasingly owns the intercompany reconciliation, close tasks, and consolidated reporting, and the strongest setups pair the two.


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is the best financial consolidation software?**


For enterprise group consolidation, OneStream, Oracle, CCH Tagetik, and SAP Group Reporting lead; for mid-market, Planful, Prophix, and Board are strong. For automating the intercompany reconciliation, close, and consolidated reporting around a consolidation engine, Concourse is the strongest AI-agent option.


### **What is financial consolidation software?**


Financial consolidation software combines the financial results of multiple entities into group financials: it runs intercompany eliminations, multi-currency translation, and ownership accounting, then produces consolidated statements. It replaces manual spreadsheet consolidation with a controlled, repeatable, auditable process.


### **Does Concourse do financial consolidation?**


Concourse is not a consolidation engine; it does not perform statutory eliminations or currency translation. What it does is automate the work around consolidation, matching and reconciling intercompany transactions, driving the close, and producing consolidated reporting and analysis, with a human approving. Most teams run it alongside a dedicated consolidation platform.


### **What is the best consolidation software for mid-market companies?**


Mid-market groups typically look at Planful, Prophix, or Board for consolidation combined with planning, and increasingly add an AI-agent layer like Concourse to automate the intercompany reconciliation and close work that consumes the most time.


## **The bottom line**


Financial consolidation software ranges from deep enterprise EPM platforms to mid-market CPM suites, and the right one depends on the complexity of your group and the ERP you already run. OneStream, Oracle, CCH Tagetik, and SAP anchor the enterprise; Planful, Prophix, and Board serve the mid-market.


The bigger shift is the separation of the consolidation engine from the manual work around it. If you want AI agents to take on the intercompany reconciliation, close, and consolidated reporting, with every number traceable and audit-ready,[book a demo of Concourse](https://www.concourse.ai/) and put an agent on your group close.
